description:
Found by the reviewing session at the s540d merge review (s542).  PRE-EXISTING on main 00c6f785; s540d`s const-fold HIDES it for a LITERAL constant (the fold reads the record in force at the use) and leaves it for every non-literal one and under PCL_OPT=-const-fold / PCL_OPT=none -- which is how it was seen: the registry rule "PCL_OPT=none must RUN identically" fails on this shape.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | main | the s540d tree):
  package Foo; use constant X => 2 + 3; use constant Y => "lit"; sub get { X } sub gety { Y }
  package Bar; sub X { "barsub" } sub Y { "barsuby" }
  package main;
  print Foo::get(), " ", Foo::gety(), "\n";
  perl: `5 lit`     main: `X Y`     s540d tree: `X lit`  (and `X Y` under PCL_OPT=-const-fold)
Without the `package Bar` line every tree prints `5 lit`.

SUSPECT (not confirmed): the pre-merge of sub declarations registers Bar`s `sub X` (no prototype) so that the bare `X` in Foo`s body no longer finds Foo`s `()` constant record -- a flat (package-blind) prototype entry overwritten by the later package`s, or a `callable in this package?` question answered by the LAST record instead of the one for the use`s package.  THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: `./pl2cl` on the reproducer and read what `sub get` lowers to ("X" vs `(pl-X)`), then swap the two package blocks (Bar first): if Foo::get() is then right, the record is overwritten in source order; if still wrong, the lookup is package-blind.

WHY IT MATTERS: constants named like another class`s method are ordinary (`use constant DEBUG => $ENV{X}` in one package, `sub DEBUG` in another, one file with several packages).  Guard: a row in Pl/t/constant-scope-01.t (perl-probed), both package orders, literal and non-literal, default and PCL_OPT=-const-fold.

=== DONE (s543b) ===
Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16, WIP 70ca2e26.  MEASURED (the task's swap): the Bar-first order was right -- the package-blind scan
answered "yes" by luck -- so the shadowing is order-dependent: PExpr::_bareword_callable_here scanned the file's declared
subs PACKAGE-BLIND and a LATER package's `sub X` answered "not-yet" before the per-package prototype record was asked.
FIX (Pl): when the current package records the name itself, another package's declaration is skipped.  Probes
p4/shapes/*.pl, 14 shapes x {default, -const-fold, none}: 13 = perl; the 14th (main bare-calls a sub of ANOTHER
package, no own record: the package-blind "yes" half) filed #5124 (LOUD).  Guard Pl/t/constant-scope-01.t rows 14-18
(fail on c5f618f2).  The gate-SET scan (both populations, base vs tree) and the full sweep: docs/session-log.md
"Session s543b".


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-100 `64353611` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-21; s543b): a bare name the current package records resolves against that record; guard Pl/t/constant-scope-01.t rows 14-18.  The package-blind `yes` half is #5124 (LOUD).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a `use constant X` used bare in ITS OWN package becomes the STRING "X" when a LATER package of the same file defines `sub X` -- `package Foo; use constant X => 2 + 3; sub get { X }  package Bar; sub X { ... }` makes Foo::get() return "X" (perl 5)
